The intervening masked load is discarded by PLA, so the old high nibble is not cleared here. Decrement budget $7FA4. While it remains nonnegative, increment a nonzero A by one; exhausted budget or zero A returns unchanged. The decrement still occurs for a zero input. Replace WorkingRecordB with X while preserving the old header across D6BC. A negative old header skips action feedback; otherwise run A708/EC2C/EC3B. Both paths finish through A711 in the active A000 view. Replace field $70DE when A is at least its current value and return. Smaller A leaves the field unchanged. Choose a field through 963B, add fifteen to indexed $70A9 and store it. If the low nibble becomes zero, clear $710B and apply header $82 through 960C. Otherwise continue the actor-field recalculation. Build a pointer to $70AC plus three times field index $7FE3, then copy the three-byte selected value $7FDD..$7FDF into that actor field in descending Y order. The preceding selection establishes the valid field index. Clear the selected three-byte value at $7FDD and visit category selectors three down to zero through 884C. Skip zero category values. D716 with factor twelve plus three times the selector addresses a three-byte record at 96AD; reverse its byte order into $7FE0..$7FE2. Compare from high byte down, replacing the selected value and category index on a greater or equal record. Finish by converting the winning index through 9698. Shift field $70A8 right once per winning category index plus one, starting A at $FF and adding outgoing bits through carry. Store the resulting byte in $7FE3 as the index used by the following packed-field update. Values depend on the caller's bounded category contract. Refresh state and scan eight slots. A negative second header byte with nonzero header $DC returns immediately. Exhausting slots reports selector $26 and continues actor-field recalculation. Use field $709F minus thirteen as the limited increment budget $7FA4 and category two as X. Category-one table values at 9719/9720/9727 are passed through 9625 two, two and one times respectively, then placed in the high nibbles of $70C3/$70C4/$70C5. Corresponding category-two tables at 9735/973C/9743 supply the ORed low values. Clear field $70DE, then fold table values for category two, zero, one and three through the maximum helper 9632. Save nonzero ID in $7EE6 and test it through A524/A6EB. A set low result bit reports selector $32; otherwise continue with packed slot membership. Form a rotated mask from $EF for the matched position, clear that membership bit in WorkingSlotHeaderThird and decrement WorkingSlotHeader. If no upper membership bits remain, clear the header entirely. Commit through A278, refresh slot displays/state and join the phase-six continuation at A144. Use the incoming zero flag from the slot-count update: zero clears WorkingSlotHeader, nonzero preserves it. Both paths commit through A278. Carry set skips directly to cleanup. regions.summary: Choose menu template ten or seven, save it in the menu byte and tail-call the banked template service. Choose a descriptor, reject unavailable nonnegative records outside the permitted IDs and prepare category fields. Read and halve its price, save the 24-bit amount and request confirmation. Cancel/retry paths share the menu loop; confirmation proceeds to the banked action window. Render the two-choice operation menu. Choice one enters the resource randomizer; choice zero enters descriptor selection. Hide the cursor during the operation and repeat according to its carry result; out-of-domain input takes the common cancellation display. Preserve the descriptor ID, clear the working ID and, when its flags are negative, temporarily install physical bank 2 through $92EB. The following direct action call runs under that bank context.

Run six outer stages with three-frame phase count, descending source offset and shared sprite/palette updates. Rebuild the palette row and decrement its offset by three between stages; hide remaining cells at completion. Copy 21 source bytes to every fourth OAM byte, with the companion row supplying the next byte in each cell. X/Y counters bound the two-row transfer. Run nine backward palette steps at six-frame intervals and hide cells from index four afterward. Use the current phase to select one of three twelve-byte tile groups, writing every fourth OAM byte. Decrement and wrap the phase to three. Build 22 pairs of OAM cells from coordinate/tile rows. The second set lies $58 OAM bytes later and uses attribute $43 instead of $03, giving a distinct reflected presentation. Point at $03D9, copy three sequential colors from the ROM row and advance the source cursor. Queue the palette update before returning. Wait 32 frames through the shared timing service and return. Run a fixed series of timed sprite and palette stages, ending with the small four-cell rise/flash animation. Each helper owns its finite counters and ordinary return. Copy 72 OAM bytes from the ROM row, then hide all cells starting at index eighteen. Copy 22 source bytes into OAM at stride four, starting at caller X. The second call continues with its updated X and source Y. Copy one three-byte palette group, subtract three from the 16-bit source, flush/wait and repeat X times. Configure a three-color destination and forward palette source, then run ten six-frame palette steps. Run descending phases that step through palette triplets and cell animation. Explicit $18, four-step and sign tests bound the choreography and its final palette update. Build twelve OAM cells backward from four parallel ROM rows for Y, tile, attributes and X, preserving the finite table domain. Repeat three sprite-tile toggles, palette updates and twelve-frame waits. Queue the current palette update and wait six frames. Configure a three-color palette destination and run three backward steps with a sixteen-frame delay. Toggle the first four tile indices and interleave timed palette changes. Decrement their Y coordinates in groups of four, with finite delay and phase counters, then return. Return three times the palette phase in X. Convert the current phase to a triplet offset, copy colors backward to $03D9, cycle sprite tiles and wait ten frames after queuing the palette. Convert A to a four-byte OAM offset and fill all remaining Y bytes with $F8, wrapping X to terminate. Copy the coordinate source to two interleaved OAM columns, load the two special endpoint values and wait twelve frames. Repeat five palette/delay phases starting at palette-source offset zero. XOR the saved tile value with $35 and write it to the tile byte of the first four OAM cells. Walk four palette groups in four-byte steps and fill their three color bytes with $0F, preserving each group's first entry. Configure the second palette destination and run five backward triplet steps at a 54-frame delay, then hide all OAM cells. Queue the palette update and wait the frame count in scratch $04. The $9C30 entry accepts its count directly in X. Run four repetitions of the shared second-presentation palette/animation phase. Run four forward three-color palette steps at a sixteen-frame interval. Copy sixteen OAM bytes for four cells from the dedicated ROM row. Alternate two three-color palette states three times, flushing each through the six-frame timing helper. Toggle tile state and walk the explicit three-color fade states with timed animation calls. Finally hide the first four OAM cells with Y=$F8. Run the second fixed sprite/palette choreography through its eight ordinary helpers; no dynamic command-stream interpretation is implied. Point the palette update at $03D5 and join the shared triplet loader. Repeat ten alternations between two pairs of 21-entry OAM source rows, waiting 32 frames after each copy. Copy 35 cells backward into OAM. Separate ROM rows supply X, tile and Y; every cell receives attribute one. Each cell occupies four bytes. Set the palette update flag to one and return. Walk palette offsets and 24 timed phases, cycle sprite tiles and choose alternate coordinate rows from the phase bits. The descending outer stage counter controls the shorter final pass. Copy three colors from the alternate source row to $03DD and queue the palette update. Queue the current palette and wait ten frames. Copy three colors from the first palette row at the saved offset to $03DD, then queue the palette update. Run nine later palette/delay phases, waiting for the source cursor to reach the required offset before each phase. Copy one three-byte palette group, advance the 16-bit source by three, flush/wait and repeat X times. Preserve the counter around the timing helper. units.name: B50RunFirstPresentationSequence
units.summary: Run a fixed series of timed sprite and palette stages, ending with the small four-cell rise/flash animation. Each helper owns its finite counters and ordinary return.

units.name: B50AlternatePresentationOamRows
units.summary: Repeat ten alternations between two pairs of 21-entry OAM source rows, waiting 32 frames after each copy.

units.name: B50WaitPresentationThirtyTwoFrames
units.summary: Wait 32 frames through the shared timing service and return.

units.name: B50FlashPresentationPalette
units.summary: Alternate two three-color palette states three times, flushing each through the six-frame timing helper.

units.name: B50FlushPaletteAndWaitSixFrames
units.summary: Queue the current palette update and wait six frames.

units.name: B50RunReverseLongPaletteSequence
units.summary: Configure a three-color palette destination and run three backward steps with a sixteen-frame delay.

units.name: B50CopyEighteenPresentationCells
units.summary: Copy 72 OAM bytes from the ROM row, then hide all cells starting at index eighteen.

units.name: B50RunForwardLongPaletteSequence
units.summary: Run four forward three-color palette steps at a sixteen-frame interval.

units.name: B50RunReverseShortPaletteSequence
units.summary: Run nine backward palette steps at six-frame intervals and hide cells from index four afterward.

units.name: B50CopyFourPresentationCells
units.summary: Copy sixteen OAM bytes for four cells from the dedicated ROM row.

units.name: B50AnimateFourCellRiseAndFlash
units.summary: Toggle the first four tile indices and interleave timed palette changes. Decrement their Y coordinates in groups of four, with finite delay and phase counters, then return.

units.name: B50RunSecondPresentationSequence
units.summary: Run the second fixed sprite/palette choreography through its eight ordinary helpers; no dynamic command-stream interpretation is implied.

units.name: B50BuildSecondPresentationCells
units.summary: Build twelve OAM cells backward from four parallel ROM rows for Y, tile, attributes and X, preserving the finite table domain.

units.name: B50RunInitialSecondPalettePhases
units.summary: Repeat five palette/delay phases starting at palette-source offset zero.

units.name: B50RunRemainingSecondPalettePhases
units.summary: Run nine later palette/delay phases, waiting for the source cursor to reach the required offset before each phase.

units.name: B50FadeAndHideFirstFourCells
units.summary: Toggle tile state and walk the explicit three-color fade states with timed animation calls. Finally hide the first four OAM cells with Y=$F8.

units.name: B50FlushPaletteAndWaitTenFrames
units.summary: Queue the current palette and wait ten frames.

units.name: B50RunFourSecondPalettePhases
units.summary: Run four repetitions of the shared second-presentation palette/animation phase.

units.name: B50BuildMirroredPresentationCells
units.summary: Build 22 pairs of OAM cells from coordinate/tile rows. The second set lies $58 OAM bytes later and uses attribute $43 instead of $03, giving a distinct reflected presentation.

units.name: B50AnimateStaggeredPaletteTriplets
units.summary: Run descending phases that step through palette triplets and cell animation. Explicit $18, four-step and sign tests bound the choreography and its final palette update.

units.name: B50AnimateSecondPresentationFinale
units.summary: Walk palette offsets and 24 timed phases, cycle sprite tiles and choose alternate coordinate rows from the phase bits. The descending outer stage counter controls the shorter final pass.

units.name: B50RunThirdPresentationSequence
units.summary: Run the descending palette/sprite sequence, wait sixteen frames and finish with the final palette row.

units.name: B50RunDescendingPresentationStages
units.summary: Run six outer stages with three-frame phase count, descending source offset and shared sprite/palette updates. Rebuild the palette row and decrement its offset by three between stages; hide remaining cells at completion.

units.name: B50RunFinalReversePaletteSequence
units.summary: Configure the second palette destination and run five backward triplet steps at a 54-frame delay, then hide all OAM cells.

units.name: B50CopyPairedOamCoordinateRows
units.summary: Copy 21 source bytes to every fourth OAM byte, with the companion row supplying the next byte in each cell. X/Y counters bound the two-row transfer.

units.name: B50SelectFirstPaletteDestination
units.summary: Point the palette update at $03D5 and join the shared triplet loader.

units.name: B50LoadPresentationPaletteTriplet
units.summary: Point at $03D9, copy three sequential colors from the ROM row and advance the source cursor. Queue the palette update before returning.

units.name: B50LoadAlternatePaletteTriplet
units.summary: Copy three colors from the alternate source row to $03DD and queue the palette update.

units.name: B50RunTimedPresentationPhase
units.summary: Repeat three sprite-tile toggles, palette updates and twelve-frame waits.

units.name: B50CycleTwelvePresentationTiles
units.summary: Use the current phase to select one of three twelve-byte tile groups, writing every fourth OAM byte. Decrement and wrap the phase to three.

units.name: B50LoadReversePaletteAndAnimate
units.summary: Convert the current phase to a triplet offset, copy colors backward to $03D9, cycle sprite tiles and wait ten frames after queuing the palette.

units.name: B50MultiplyPalettePhaseByThree
units.summary: Return three times the palette phase in X.

units.name: B50LoadFinalPresentationPaletteTriplet
units.summary: Copy three colors from the first palette row at the saved offset to $03DD, then queue the palette update.

units.name: B50CopyPairedOamRowsAndWait
units.summary: Copy the coordinate source to two interleaved OAM columns, load the two special endpoint values and wait twelve frames.

units.name: B50CopyTwentyTwoOamStrideBytes
units.summary: Copy 22 source bytes into OAM at stride four, starting at caller X. The second call continues with its updated X and source Y.

units.name: B50FlushPaletteAndWait
units.summary: Queue the palette update and wait the frame count in scratch $04. The $9C30 entry accepts its count directly in X.

units.name: B50QueuePresentationPaletteUpdate
units.summary: Set the palette update flag to one and return.

units.name: B50ToggleFourPresentationTiles
units.summary: XOR the saved tile value with $35 and write it to the tile byte of the first four OAM cells.

units.name: B50HidePresentationCellsFromIndex
units.summary: Convert A to a four-byte OAM offset and fill all remaining Y bytes with $F8, wrapping X to terminate.

units.name: B50RunForwardPaletteTriplets
units.summary: Copy one three-byte palette group, advance the 16-bit source by three, flush/wait and repeat X times. Preserve the counter around the timing helper.

units.name: B50RunReversePaletteTriplets
units.summary: Copy one three-byte palette group, subtract three from the 16-bit source, flush/wait and repeat X times.
